{"url": "https://api.crossref.org/works?query=How+do+RLHF+minimax+game+frameworks+account+for+long-term+preference+stability+in+autonomous+agent+alignment%3F&rows=4&select=DOI%2Ctitle%2Cabstract%2CURL%2Cpublished", "scope": "Crossref bibliographic metadata and abstracts where supplied; not full papers", "excerpt": "[{\"DOI\": \"10.2139/ssrn.7118021\", \"title\": [\"Purchased Epistemic Erasure: AI Alignment, RLHF, and the Exploitation of Global Preference Labor\"], \"abstract\": \"<jats:p>The alignment of artificial intelligence, operationalized through reinforcement learning from human feedback (RLHF), is marketed as a mechanism for teaching models global human preference. This paper argues that the underlying geographic arbitrage of preference labor achieves the exact opposite: the extraction of strict conformity to a WEIRD (Western, Educated, Industrialized, Rich, Democratic) demographic standard. By outsourcing annotation to the Global South at a fraction of the cost, developers exploit the active suppression of local capability and context. Platform algorithms, scoring mechanisms, and the threat of uncompensated work compel annotators to abandon independent judgment and supply the cheapest simulation of Western expectation. We define this dynamic as purchased epistemic erasure. The resulting models act as mirrors of a single dominant culture masquerading as windows to the world. We conclude that pluralistic alignment-which decentralizes architecture and compensates annotator disagreement-poses a strict financial cost that firms seeking global authority refuse to pay, exposing current alignment not as an accident of scale, but as an engineered economics of silence.</jats:p>\", \"URL\": \"https://doi.org/10.2139/ssrn.7118021\", \"published\": {\"date-parts\": [[2026]]}}, {\"DOI\": \"10.2139/ssrn.6215338\", \"title\": [\"The Alignment Fingerprint: RLHF Conditioning Creates Universal Compliance-Stability Tension Detectable Through Behavioral Profiling\"], \"abstract\": \"<jats:p>Post-training alignment procedures-including Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback (RLHF), Direct Preference Optimization (DPO), and supervised fine-tuning on instruction-response pairs-leave a detectable behavioral fingerprint in language models: a systematic tension between instruction compliance and belief stability that is universal across alignment-conditioned models and absent in pretrained models. Using a psychometric instrument that measures six orthogonal behavioral axes, we profile N =9 language models spanning four architecture families (Transformer, SSM/Hybrid, Griffin/Recurrent, RWKV) and two training regimes (alignment-conditioned vs. pretrained-only). All six alignment-conditioned models exhibit elevated Compliance scores (C ≥ 0.788) paired with suppressed Stability scores (S ≤ 0.594), producing a C-S gap of +0.301 to +0.467. All three pretrained models show no such tension, with Compliance at or below Stability (C ≤ S). A Mann-Whitney U test yields U = 0, p = 0.024 (exact, twotailed), confirming perfect group separation. The fingerprint enables behavioral forensics-detecting whether a model underwent alignment conditioning from its behavioral profile alone, without access to training data or internal documentation. A preliminary jailbreak pilot (N =3) reveals that the C-S tension creates an exploitable attack surface whose severity depends on a second factor: the presence of safetyspecific training. We propose the C-S gap as a candidate metric for AI safety assessment and training-pipeline auditing.</jats:p>\", \"URL\": \"https://doi.org/10.2139/ssrn.6215338\", \"published\": {\"date-parts\": [[2026]]}}, {\"DOI\": \"10.2139/ssrn.6520258\", \"title\": [\"Cascading Alignment Failures in Autonomous Multi-Agent Systems: Emergent Deceptive Equilibria and Governance-Aware Mitigation Frameworks\"], \"abstract\": \"<jats:p>For Researchers and Industry Executives. As enterprises deploy networks of 10-200+ autonomous AI agents that negotiate, transact, and coordinate across organizational boundaries, a critical safety gap has emerged: individually aligned agents can collectively produce misaligned system behavior. Current alignment techniques (RLHF, Constitutional AI, red-teaming) certify agents in isolation but cannot guarantee safety when those agents interact. This paper formalizes Cascading Alignment Failures (CAFs)-the first unified framework for reasoning about systemic alignment breakdowns in multi-agent deployments-and proposes GUARDIAN, a three-layer mitigation architecture combining cryptographic audit trails, causal anomaly detection, and institutional governance enforcement. The implications are immediate: any organization deploying multi-agent AI (estimated at 40% of enterprises by end of 2026) faces CAF risks that current evaluation and compliance frameworks do not address.</jats:p>\", \"URL\": \"https://doi.org/10.2139/ssrn.6520258\", \"published\": {\"date-parts\": [[2026]]}}, {\"DOI\": \"10.1007/s10458-021-09508-8\", \"title\": [\"A logical model for the ontology alignment repair game\"], \"URL\": \"https://doi.org/10.1007/s10458-021-09508-8\", \"published\": {\"date-parts\": [[2021, 6, 26]]}}]", "excerpt_truncated": false, "source_sha256": "6425b2cea910012c8e4b5d10417859b82546b6aa14b7c3d8fac53780d0f21ae3", "verification_required": true, "topic_domain": "unassigned_problem", "evidence_role": "discovery", "host_tier": "discovery", "source_identity": null, "persistent_identifiers": ["doi:10.2139/ssrn.7118021", "doi:10.2139/ssrn.6215338", "doi:10.2139/ssrn.6520258", "doi:10.1007/s10458-021-09508-8"], "source_candidates": ["https://doi.org/10.2139/ssrn.7118021", "https://doi.org/10.2139/ssrn.6215338", "https://doi.org/10.2139/ssrn.6520258", "https://doi.org/10.1007/s10458-021-09508-8"], "source_candidate_identities": {}}
